problems.title: PCM evaluation uses a different stochastic law
claim: Appendix E.1 describes zero-mean Gaussian error with one cubic standard-deviation polynomial.
analysis: Current Appendix E.1 specifies \(\widehat W=W+\eta\), with zero-mean Gaussian \(\eta\) and one cubic standard-deviation rule. The current add_PCM_noise rescales conductance, forces output zero when \(|g|<0.6\), uses one polynomial up to \(52.5\), and another above it. A legal row with maximum absolute weight \(1\) and a nonzero entry \(0.3/180\) has normalized conductance just below \(0.3\), so that entry is deterministically set to zero: its error has nonzero mean and zero variance. Unit conversion and coefficient rounding cannot make this a zero-mean Gaussian. The high-conductance branch does approximately match the printed polynomial; the discrepancy is localized, and no historical benchmark effect is measured.
result: The stated local claim or source contract fails as described. Its effect on historical experiment scores is unmeasured.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Specify the piecewise evaluation law, normalization and threshold, and bind the reported hardware results to the exact author version used.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.

problems.title: The clipping contribution is confounded
problems.source_location: Current paper, Appendix C.3 and Table 13, p. 24; clipping interpretation, p. 6 and Appendix D.1, p. 25.
claim: The comparison interprets Table 13 as clipping contributing more than training noise.
analysis: Table 13 gives printed noisy-evaluation averages \(62.92\), \(65.44\) and \(65.96\). The first change adds a complete adaptation/training and quantization pipeline including clipping; the second adds training noise within that already adapted pipeline. If \(A(B,C,N)\) denotes the score with non-clipping adaptation \(B\), clipping \(C\), and noise \(N\), the table supplies \(A(0,0,0)\), \(A(1,1,0)\) and \(A(1,1,1)\), but omits \(A(1,0,0)\). Consequently the isolated clipping effect \(A(1,1,0)-A(1,0,0)\) may be larger, smaller or negative while retaining all three observations. The \(2.52\)-point composite gain and \(0.52\)-point conditional-noise gain do not identify that comparison. The SNR/quantization mechanisms remain compatible with clipping helping in practice.
result: This remains a bounded scope or unresolved-source concern; broader experimental invalidity is not established.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Narrow attribution to the compared composite settings or provide matched component ablations.

problems.title: The displayed training entry does not convert analog layers
problems.source_location: Current author src/analog_foundation_models/train.py, model construction and Trainer call; utils/train_utils.py, clipping hook; utils/aihwkit_utils.py; example.py inference conversion.
claim: The public training pipeline is intended to implement hardware-aware analog training.
analysis: The current training entry loads an ordinary AutoModelForCausalLM from the standard base model and passes it to CustomTrainer without analog-layer conversion or use of create_rpu_config. The Trainer clips only if the model exposes analog_layers; its shown path does not create those layers. The inference example separately performs conversion, which does not retroactively change the training path. This establishes a public-entry gap rather than proving the final paper’s internal training used no analog operators; the pinned public head predates the final manuscript.
result: The stated local claim or source contract fails as described. Its effect on historical experiment scores is unmeasured.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Provide the intended analog-layer conversion and run configuration in the training entry; no restored full-model training result is asserted.
